text:
Tom: FYI euw2 experienced a near-oom event just now. GPUs hit sustained mem pressure, we saw heavy KV cache evictions + throttle spikes. Not fully OOM but close.
Maya: saw the alerts. Autoscaler spun up nodes but eviction rate outpaced new capacity.
Arun: any recent config changes?
Tom: we re-enabled prefetching and bumped kv_cache_window to 45s for latency tests earlier today.
Priya: ooof, that change was to reduce cold-start for chat flows — thought it was safe.
Zoe: workload changed too: long-chat sessions from the promotional campaign have higher seq lengths + prefix reuse, so prefetching inflated active KV state.
capacity-bot: Autoscaler event: scale up +4 g4dn nodes at 1892345682. Thresholds: gpu_mem_pressure=0.82 -> 0.95.
Arun: can you paste the eviction logs?
Tom: simple excerpt below from node-7 log:
```
WARNING kv_cache: eviction triggered. active_kv=132MB -> 16MB after prune
ERROR mem: available_gpu=210MB, request=320MB, throttling=true
```
Maya: looks like prefetching allocated per-request KV entries without considering concurrent sessions. Windowing + long-chats multiplied state.
Priya: that explains why autoscaler couldn't keep up — per-request memory was unexpectedly high. Forecast didn't include promo long-chats footprint.
Zoe: our evals used avg seq len 1.8k, promo traffic is 5-6k for some flows. Need to update model for seq length distrib.
Arun: short-term: rollback prefetch flag, reduce kv_cache_window to 10s, lower per-req kv-reservation. Long-term: make prefetching memory-aware and add backpressure signals.
Tom: rolling rollback now: `PATCH /config/prefetch_enabled=false` -> deploying to euw2.
deploy-bot: deploy started by Tom at 1892345721 - rolling to euw2 (4 pods at a time)
capacity-bot: Autoscaler manual override recommended. Current headroom 5% in euw2.
Maya: we need an immediate capacity buffer for the next 72h — recommend reserving +40% GPU hours for euw2 to cover forecast variance.
Priya: cost impact estimate? +40% reserved for 72h ~ ~1200 GPU-hours -> ~estimated $48k. (rough).
Zoe: vs risk: another near-oom during promo would cause degraded p99 latency and customer impact. I vote reserve. :thumbsup:
Arun: add action items: 1) revert prefetch (done), 2) kv_cache_window=10s (in flight), 3) update capacity forecast to include heavy-tail seq lengths and promo multipliers, 4) implement memory-aware prefetch with soft limits and backpressure, 5) run chaos tests with long-chat sim.
Tom: saving full logs & a perf trace to S3: s3://redwood-ops/euw2/prefetch-near-oom/1892345678/
Maya: I'll open a short postmortem doc and link runbook changes.
Priya: also add a billing signal to finance: reserve cost + notify sales about potential customer impact if scaled back.
Zoe: ML note — we can add a lightweight seq-length estimator at the request frontdoor to gate prefetching for large chats. Low-latency and cheap.
Tom: next steps: keep prefetch disabled for 48h, monitor evictions and p99, commit forecast adjustments by EOD, and schedule a follow-up retro tomorrow 10:30am CET.
Maya: agreed. tagging @arun @priya for the retro. :eyes:
Arun: copying config diff to PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/configs/pulls/482 (prefetch revert + kv tuning)
deploy-bot: deploy completed at 1892345784 - euw2 prefetch flag rolled back
Maya: current metrics: eviction rate down 78%, p99 latency improving, memory headroom stable ~28%. Will update the postmortem with graphs.
Tom: thanks all — good catch. We'll fold learnings into capacity forecasting (heavy-tail seq lengths + prefetch memory multiplier).
